questions.problem:
A nationwide study found that $38%$ of families own a pet. If a town randomly samples $200$ families, find a normal approximation for the probability that more than $80$ of them are pet owners. You may assume that the population size is significantly larger than the sample size.

*Note: $Φ(z)$ is the cumulative distribution function for the standard normal distribution.*
questions.worked_solution:
Given a population in which a proportion $p$ of the population has a particular characteristic, the sampling distribution of the sample proportion $\overset{^}{\,p}$ can be approximated as

$$
\overset{^}{\,p}∼N(p,\frac{p(1-p)}{n}),
$$

where the sample size $n$ is much smaller than the population size, $np>5,$ and $n(1-p)>5.$

In our case

- the sample size is $n=200,$ and

- the population proportion is $p=0.38.$

Now, since

$$
np=200(0.38)=76>5
$$

and

$$
n(1-p)=200(1-0.38)=124>5,
$$

and $n=200$ is much smaller than the population size, we can apply the above approximation.

The sampling distribution of the sample proportion, in this case, can be approximated as

$$
\begin{aligned}\overset{^}{\,p} & ∼N(p,\frac{p(1-p)}{n}) \\  & ∼N(0.38,\frac{0.38(1-0.38)}{200}) \\  & ∼N(0.38,0.0012).\end{aligned}
$$

Next, we determine the probability we wish to find. If more than $80$ families in the sample own a pet, then 

$$
\overset{^}{\,p}>\frac{80}{200}=0.4.
$$

Hence, the probability we wish to find is
$P(\overset{^}{\,p}>0.4).$
So, we convert $\overset{^}{\,p}$ to a standard normal random variable by $z$-scoring:

$$
\begin{aligned}P(\overset{^}{\,p}>0.4) & =P(Z>\frac{0.4-0.38}{\sqrt{0.0012}}) \\  & ≈P(Z>0.58) \\  & =1-P(Z<0.58) \\  & =1-Φ(0.58).\end{aligned}
$$

questions.problem:
Suppose we take a random sample of size $n=88$ from a population where $44%$ of the population has a particular characteristic. Find a normal approximation for the probability that more than $52%$ of the sample has the characteristic. You may assume that the population size is significantly larger than the sample size.

*Hint: $Φ(z)$ is the cumulative distribution function for the standard normal distribution.*
questions.worked_solution:

$$
\overset{^}{\,p}∼N(p,\frac{p(1-p)}{n}),
$$

where the sample size $n$ is much smaller than the population size, $np>5,$ and $n(1-p)>5.$

In our case

- the sample size is $n=88,$ and

- the population proportion is $p=0.44.$

Now, since

$$
np=88(0.44)=38.72>5
$$

and

$$
n(1-p)=88(1-0.44)=49.28>5,
$$

and $n=88$ is much smaller than the population size, we can apply the above approximation.

The sampling distribution of the sample proportion, in this case, can be approximated as

$$
\begin{aligned}\overset{^}{\,p} & ∼N(p,\frac{p(1-p)}{n}) \\  & ∼N(0.44,\frac{0.44(1-0.44)}{88}) \\  & ∼N(0.44,0.0028).\end{aligned}
$$

The probability we wish to find is
$P(\overset{^}{\,p}>0.52).$
So, we convert $\overset{^}{\,p}$ to a standard normal random variable by $z$-scoring:

$$
\begin{aligned}P(\overset{^}{\,p}>0.52) & =P(Z>\frac{0.52-0.44}{\sqrt{0.0028}}) \\  & ≈P(Z>1.51) \\  & =1-P(Z\le 1.51) \\  & =1-Φ(1.51)\end{aligned}
$$

Find a normal approximation for the probability that more than $70%$ but less than $80%$ of the sample has the characteristic. You may assume that the population size is significantly larger than the sample size. *Hint: Two tables of values of $Φ(z)$ for different values of $z$ are given below, where $Φ(z)$ is the cumulative distribution function for the standard normal distribution. *

questions.worked_solution:
Given a population in which a proportion $p$ of the population has a particular characteristic, the sampling distribution of the sample proportion $\overset{^}{\,p}$ can be approximated as

$$
\overset{^}{\,p}∼N(p,\frac{p(1-p)}{n}),
$$

where the sample size $n$ is much smaller than the population size, $np>5,$ and $n(1-p)>5.$

In our case

- the sample size is $n=96,$ and

- the population proportion is $p=0.72.$

Now, since

$$
np=96(0.72)=69.12>5
$$

and

$$
n(1-p)=96(1-0.72)=26.88>5,
$$

and $n=96$ is much smaller than the population size, we can apply the above approximation.

The sampling distribution of the sample proportion, in this case, can be approximated as

$$
\begin{aligned}\overset{^}{\,p} & ∼N(p,\frac{p(1-p)}{n}) \\  & ∼N(0.72,\frac{0.72(1-0.72)}{96}) \\  & ∼N(0.72,0.0021).\end{aligned}
$$

The probability we wish to find is
$P(0.7<\overset{^}{\,p}\le 0.8).$
So, we convert $\overset{^}{\,p}$ to a standard normal random variable by $z$-scoring:

$$
\begin{aligned}P(0.7<\overset{^}{\,p}<0.8) & =P(\frac{0.7-0.72}{\sqrt{0.0021}}<Z\le \frac{0.8-0.72}{\sqrt{0.0021}}) \\  & ≈P(-0.44<Z\le 1.75) \\  & =P(Z\le 1.75)-P(Z\le -0.44) \\  & =Φ(1.75)-Φ(-0.44)\end{aligned}
$$

From the table, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}Φ(1.75) & =0.9599 \\ Φ(-0.44) & =0.3300.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore,

$$
\begin{aligned}P(0.7<\overset{^}{\,p}<0.8) & =Φ(1.75)-Φ(-0.44) \\  & =0.9599-0.3300 \\  & =0.6299.\end{aligned}
$$

A fitness center has $1600$ members, $480$ of which play tennis. If the center randomly samples $60$ members, find a normal approximation for the probability that more than $24$ members in the sample play tennis. You may assume that the population size is significantly larger than the sample size.

*Hint: A table of values of $Φ(z)$ for different values of $z$ are given below, where $Φ(z)$ is the cumulative distribution function for the standard normal distribution.*

| $z$ | $\,0.07\,$ | $\,0.08\,$ | $\,0.09\,$ |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $\,1.5\,$ | $\,0.9418\,$ | $\,0.9429\,$ | $\,0.9441\,$ |
| $\,1.6\,$ | $\,0.9525\,$ | $\,0.9535\,$ | $\,0.9545\,$ |
| $\,1.7\,$ | $\,0.9616\,$ | $\,0.9625\,$ | $\,0.9633\,$ |
questions.worked_solution:
Given a population in which a proportion $p$ of the population has a particular characteristic, the sampling distribution of the sample proportion $\overset{^}{\,p}$ can be approximated as

$$
\overset{^}{\,p}∼N(p,\frac{p(1-p)}{n}),
$$

where the sample size $n$ is much smaller than the population size, $np>5,$ and $n(1-p)>5.$

In our case

- the sample size is $n=60,$ and

- the population proportion is $p=\frac{480}{1600}=0.3.$

Now, since

$$
np=60(0.3)=18>5
$$

and

$$
n(1-p)=60(1-0.3)=42>5,
$$

and the $n=60$ is much smaller than the population size, we can apply the above approximation.

The sampling distribution of the sample proportion, in this case, can be approximated as

$$
\begin{aligned}\overset{^}{\,p} & ∼N(p,\frac{p(1-p)}{n}) \\  & ∼N(0.3,\frac{0.3(1-0.3)}{60}) \\  & ∼N(0.3,0.0035).\end{aligned}
$$

Next, we determine the probability we wish to find. If more than $24$ members in the sample play tennis, then

$$
\begin{aligned}\overset{^}{\,p} & >\frac{24}{60}=0.4\end{aligned}
$$

Hence, the probability we wish to find is
$P(\overset{^}{\,p}>0.4).$
So, we convert $\overset{^}{\,p}$ to a standard normal random variable by $z$-scoring:

$$
\begin{aligned}P(\overset{^}{\,p}>0.4) & =P(Z>\frac{0.4-0.3}{\sqrt{0.0035}}) \\  & ≈P(Z>1.69) \\  & =1-P(Z\le 1.69) \\  & =1-Φ(1.69)\end{aligned}
$$

From the table, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}Φ(1.69)=0.9545.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore,

$$
\begin{aligned}P(0.4\le \overset{^}{\,p}) & =1-Φ(1.69) \\  & =0.0455.\end{aligned}
$$
